1 · Intro

When to use it.

A requisition is the request to recruit. It's built from a position, and it copies that position the moment you submit, so check the position first.

Vanderbilt's recruiting is outsourced to Cielo, which bills for every opening and every fill. Open only what you'll actually fill.

Use this whenAn approved position needs to be posted and recruited for.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in Oracle Recruiting. Check off each step as you go.

Before you submit

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

  • Pre-search memo from the last 12 months, with a job code that matches the position Required
  • Position description Attach

Check

Read every field back against the source document: person, effective date, position, hours, pay, and costing.

  • The position is right before you start. The requisition copies it when submitted.
  • Openings are a number, never Unlimited.
  • Location is a real work location, never United States.
  • New York: the New York candidate selection process and account VAN09.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: You.
  • Who approves: More than one opening also goes to central finance. To confirm: the approval chain for this transaction.
  • What happens next: Recruiting works the requisition. The recruiter makes the offer.

Watch-outs

  • Never select Unlimited openings.
  • Never use United States as the location.
  • New York: New York candidate selection process and account VAN09, every time.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Create a Job Requisition Based on a Position (opens in a new tab)
  • Oracle: Create a Job Requisition (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy quick guide · Hiring

Create a requisition

Use when: An approved position needs to be posted and recruited for. · System: Oracle Recruiting

  1. Check the position first.
  2. Open Hiring and click Create.
  3. Choose Standard and select the position.
  4. Requisition title: the posting title.
  5. Justification and openings.
    • Each opening is billed, and unfilled openings are billed at 50% to cancel.
    • More than one opening also goes to central finance for approval.
  6. Hiring manager and collaborators.
  7. Requisition type: Standard or Abbreviated.
    • Executive search is only for Cielo's executive search program. An outside firm (such as Korn Ferry) needs a PO requisition, not a recruiting requisition.
  8. Organization and primary location.
  9. Required details.
  10. Description: paste the position description.
  11. Offer info: workplace type.
  12. Attach the position description and pre-search memo.
  13. Configuration: candidate selection process and background check.
    • New York requires non-criminal checks before any conditional offer. The wrong process breaks that law.
  14. Click Save, then Submit.

Before you submit

  • Attach: Pre-search memo from the last 12 months, with a job code that matches the position (required). Position description (attach).
  • Check: The position is right before you start. The requisition copies it when submitted. Openings are a number, never Unlimited. Location is a real work location, never United States. New York: the New York candidate selection process and account VAN09.

Watch-outs

  • Never select Unlimited openings.
  • Never use United States as the location.
  • New York: New York candidate selection process and account VAN09, every time.

HCM Academy detailed job aid · Hiring

Creating a requisition, step by step

Step by step with screenshots. Screens from the HCM Academy training simulation of Oracle HCM. Names are fictional; check labels against Vanderbilt's Oracle.

  1. 01Check the position first.

    Confirm it has a six-digit job code and the right location and category. The requisition snapshots the position at submission and can't be changed later, and bad data flows on to the new hire.

  2. 02Open Hiring and click Create.

    Our Workforce > Hiring > Job Requisitions, then Create at the top. (Or go straight there: Our Workforce > Show More > Create Job Requisition.) You see the requisitions for your business unit, and you're a collaborator on any you create.

  3. 03Choose Standard and select the position.

    Pipeline is for recruiters only. Pick the position; its job details fill in, and the position can't be changed after this.

  4. 04Requisition title: the posting title.

    Change it to something candidates understand (for example, add Senior or Hybrid). It's only the posting title, not the business title.

  5. 05Justification and openings.

    New to the department, or replacing someone. Choose Limited and the exact number of seats. Never Unlimited.

  6. 06Hiring manager and collaborators.

    Add the hiring manager (not you, unless you are). Add collaborators who should see candidates or interview, including any HCM you work with. Hiring managers see candidates once the recruiter has reviewed them.

  7. 07Requisition type: Standard or Abbreviated.

    Standard is the full recruiting process. Abbreviated means you already have a candidate, usually internal; it must still be posted internally for five business days.

  8. 08Organization and primary location.

    Organization is always Vanderbilt. Pick the specific location (Nashville, New York, California, West Palm Beach, and so on), never United States. Location tells recruiting whether pay transparency applies; pay ranges are posted only where required (New York and California).

  9. 09Required details.

    Fill in what's required: funding source (internal, external, or both; external adds contingent funding language to the offer), driving, replacing a RIF role, fingerprinting, motor vehicle record, and work with minors. Salary range is optional. Skip Tier; it's for billing.

  10. 10Description: paste the position description.

    Paste it into the description so the recruiter can post it (they can't post from an attachment). You can write different internal and external versions. Let Skills pull through from the job architecture.

  11. 11Offer info: workplace type.

    Pick On site, Hybrid, or Remote. Skip Grades. Leave Primary work location as it is; it's overridden at hire if the person is remote.

  12. 12Attach the position description and pre-search memo.

    Central recruiting checks the memo exists, is from the last 12 months, and has the same job code as the requisition.

  13. 13Configuration: candidate selection process and background check.

    New York requisitions must use the New York candidate selection process; everything else uses Standard. Background check vendor: HireRight. Account: VAN000 for non New York, VAN09 for New York.

  14. 14Click Save, then Submit.

    Ignore the background check packages pop-up; the recruiter picks packages at the offer. Approval goes to the hiring line manager, your business unit's financial approver, then central recruiting (and central finance if more than one opening). Once approved, you and the recruiter get an email and the recruiter sets up the strategy meeting.
